key_insight: No surrogate wins universally: FNO and Latent DeepONet lead on one fracture dataset, while diffusion is most accurate but far slower on the other.
engineering_relevance: Fracture-Bench helps engineers compare surrogate accuracy and computational cost before using them for uncertainty quantification, inverse analysis or design.
method: Benchmark two phase-field regimes: 1,000 AT2 simulations and 4,000 PF-CZM simulations.
Compare FNO, DeepONet, Latent DeepONet, UNet and conditional diffusion using identical splits.
Report dataset-specific test error, training time, inference time and model size.
evidence_signal: On Dataset 1, FNO and Latent DeepONet achieve mean errors of order 10⁻⁶; on Dataset 2, diffusion has about one-sixth the UNet error but takes 706 s per prediction versus 6 ms.
watch_item: Average errors can obscure near-bifurcation failures: initial cracks less than one grid cell apart can produce qualitatively different paths, and errors concentrate after crack localization.
paper_title: Fracture-Bench: A Controlled Benchmark Suite for Machine Learning Surrogates in Phase-Field Fracture Mechanics
